div.head: VI As 8.1
div.ab: Eahtoðe, þæt we us gegaderian á emban ænne monað, gif we mágon ⁊ ǽmton habban, þa hyndenmenn ⁊ þa þe ða teoþunge bewítan, swa mid byttfyllinge swa elles swa us tóanhágie, ⁊ witen, hwæt ure gecwydræddene gelæst sy; ⁊ habban þa XII menn heora metscype tógædere ⁊ fedan hig swa swa hig sylfe wyrðe múnon, ⁊ dælon ealle þa metelafe Godes þances.

Octauum est ut conueniamus semper ad unum mensem, si possimus et licitum habeamus, per hindemen (hyndenos homines) et eos qui decimas custodiunt, sic cum bucellorum impletione sic aliter sicut poterimus, et sciamus, quid edictorum nostrorum compleatur; et habeant ipsi duodecim homines conuictum suum simul et pascant se sicut deceat, et remanens diuidant pro amore Dei.

Eahtoðe: Þæt we us gegaderian à emban ænne monað, gif we mágon ⁊ ǽmton habban, þa hyndenmenn ⁊ þa þe ða teoþunge bewitan, swa mid byttfyllinge swa elles swa us tóanhágie, ⁊ witen hwæt ure gecwydræddene gelæst sy; ⁊ habban þa XII menn heora metscype tógædere ⁊ fedan hig swa swa hig sylfe wyrðe múnon, ⁊ dælon ealle þa metelafe Godes þances.

Achtens, dass wir uns je nach einem Monat versammeln, wenn wir können und Musse haben, [nämlich] die Hundertverbandsvorsteher und die, welche die Zehntschaften beaufsichtigen, sei es beim Büttenfüllen [zum künftigen Gildenfest], sei es, wie es uns sonst passen mag, und vermerken, was von unserer Übereinkunft erfüllt worden ist; und es sollen die 12 [lies 11] Männer ihre Mahlzeit zusammen erhalten [auf Kosten der Genossenschaft] und essen, so wie sie selbst für würdig erachten, und alle die Speisereste [Armen] vertheilen um Gottes willen.

Eighthly, that we gather once a month, if we can and have leisure, [namely] the heads of the hundreds and those who supervise the tithings, whether at the filling of the butts [for a coming guild-feast] or however else it may suit us, and note what of our agreement has been fulfilled; and the 12 [read 11] men are to have their meal together [at the fellowship's expense] and feed themselves as they themselves think fit, and distribute all the leftover food [to the poor] for the love of God.

Eighth: We, the officials of the hundred-groups and those who have charge of the bodies of ten, shall assemble once every month, if we have leisure and can do so — whether it be when the butts are being filled, or on any other occasion that may be convenient for us; and we shall take cognisance of how our various statutes are being observed. Twelve men shall then have their dinners together, and they shall have such food as they themselves think right, and they shall give away all the fragments, for the love of God.

Eighthly: that we, the hundred-men and those who have charge of the tithing, shall always assemble once a month, if we can and have leisure, whether at the time of the filling of the butts or else when it suits us, and take note how our agreement is being observed; and then 12 men shall dine together and shall supply themselves as they think fitting, and distribute all the leavings for God’s sake.

Nicht alle Landfriedensbündner, auch nicht alle Gildenbürger, sondern nur als Vertreter der letzteren, vielleicht auch aller ersteren, versammelt sich monatlich jede Elfmännergruppe (ein Hyndenvorsteher und die 10 Zehnerschaftsvorsteher) und speist an Einer Tafel auf Kosten der Gilde. Q versteht richtig, ‘wir’, die Gesamtheit, sind versammelt durch (per) jene Vertreter. Falls nicht Archetyp þurh hierfür las, ist ²þa Nominativ, Apposition zu we. Solche Wendung schien Price-Thorpe [mit Unrecht] so schwierig, dass er us (als Dativ) ‘zu uns’ versteht. Aber die Gilde kann doch nicht ohne ihre Häupter als ‘wir’ befehlen. Dass ferner alle Elfergruppen [in Einem Hause?] zusammenkamen, muss verstanden werden, weil es sich nicht um Bericht über die einzelne Hundertzahl, sondern über die ganze Gilde handelt. Jedenfalls aber war die monatliche Zusammenkunft nicht (wie Kemble Saxons I 253; Hegel Städte I 27 wollen) identisch mit dem Gildenfest, für das ja das Büttenfüllen erst vorbereitend geschah; s. Gl Genossenschaft 12h

Not all the members of the peace-association, nor all the gild-burgesses, but each group of eleven (a hynden-head and the 10 tithing-heads), only as representatives of the latter and perhaps of all the former too, assembles monthly and dines at a single table at the gild’s expense. Q rightly understands that ‘we’, the whole body, are assembled through (per) those representatives. Unless the archetype read þurh here, ²þa is nominative, in apposition to we. Price-Thorpe thought [wrongly] such a turn of phrase so difficult that he takes us (as dative) to mean ‘to us’. But the gild surely cannot give orders as ‘we’ without its heads. It must further be understood that all the groups of eleven came together [in a single house?], because the matter concerns a report not on the individual hundred but on the whole gild. In any case, however, the monthly meeting was not (as Kemble Saxons I 253 and Hegel Städte I 27 would have it) identical with the gild-feast, for which, after all, the filling of the butts was only a preparation; see Gl Genossenschaft 12h
Die Morgensprache der Gilde heisst später bisweilen congregatio
The gild’s morning-speech is later sometimes called congregatio

See Gl Genossenschaft 7; ‘butt-filler’, like ‘cup-bearer’ (see that word in Gl 3), are household officials [‘cup-filling’ does not stand there and does not mean ‘drinking’; nor is a ‘cup’ in contrast to the meal of the eleven: against Marquardsen Haft 39. — From the 13th cent. the English town has fire-fighting arrangements; in 1212 London has the coopers set up water-tubs; Munim. Gildhal. ed. Riley II 88; Engl. gilds ed. T. Smith 371. 382. But filling butts with water required no such important deliberation]. The word in Q is OFr. boucel, ‘cask’ for wine and bread; Ducange s. v. botta 3; Littré s. v. boucaut

So bessern seit Marquardsen Haft 39, Kemble Saxons I 242 Neuere, mit hig XI in 3⁸ sie gleichsetzend. Der Archetyp hatte ein Zwölferkolleg im Sinne, entweder Lagamen (s. d. Gl 2—4ff.) oder Ratmannen der Stadt; s. d. Gl 19b. c. Ausgeschlossen aber scheint mir, dass das Original an eine Zwölferbehörde der Gilde oder Stadt, von jenen 11 ganz zu trennen, gedacht habe

So more recent scholars emend, since Marquardsen Haft 39 and Kemble Saxons I 242, equating them with hig XI in 3⁸. The archetype had in mind a college of twelve, either lawmen (see that word in Gl 2—4ff.) or the town’s councillors; see that word in Gl 19b. c. But it seems to me out of the question that the original was thinking of a body of twelve belonging to the gild or town, entirely separate from those 11
Das Wort ist sonst nicht belegt. Der Stil verbietet, mit Hegel dieses Hyndenmahl zu trennen von der beratenden Zusammenkunft vorigen Satzes
The word is not attested elsewhere. The style forbids separating this hynden-meal, with Hegel, from the deliberative meeting of the preceding sentence
Dies liegt im ‘Empfangen, Bekommen’ von anderer Seite
This is implied in ‘receiving, getting’ from another party
Liebermann interprets this as referring to preparations for a coming feast of the guild.
The arithmetic is rather difficult to understand. Quadr. also has duodecim homines. Liebermann emends to xi and takes þa (Quadr. ipsi) as nominative plural of the pronoun.
